warnings.warning: Equation (1) is typographically ambiguous about degree subtraction and coordinate order; verify it against a standard great-circle calculation.
Equation (10) uses a greater-than-or-equal count while the assembled program in equation (13) prints equality; decide whether quantities are minima or exact counts.
The loading program does not visibly state non-overlap, height accumulation, orientation domains, or container bounds sufficient for a complete 3D packing model.
The paper says a larger evaluation value is better although the product grows with residual dimensional gaps; confirm the ranking direction and fit interpretation.
Equation (18) sums over container index d while the displayed summand lacks d, so the allocation semantics may be duplicated or incomplete.
The full-load factor e is not defined numerically, and the printed endpoint description does not establish whether mu should be below or above one.
Focused visual review confirms the printed factor (mu-1)/2; if mu is below one, the left side becomes negative, so the sign and physical interpretation require correction.
The minimax objective appears to omit loaded return, service, recharge, and repeated-sortie time and needs a defined assignment domain.
Maximizing a positive normalized min-T term appears to reward larger transport time; the objective direction or normalization needs reconciliation.
The one-degree result depends on OCR-fragile geometry and a circular sweep abstraction; recompute with consistent kilometres and validate against the road network.
The twenty-drone calculation assumes complete 360-degree independent strips, forty minutes per degree, no charging delay, and no overlap or road-routing loss.
